h1: Combating Trafficking in Persons (CTIP) Training Practice Questions
subhead: Get instant, explained answers to CTIP training questions — recognize the indicators of human trafficking and finish your training without the guesswork.
metaTitle: CTIP Training Practice Questions & Answers | Cambo
metaDescription: Practice Combating Trafficking in Persons (CTIP) training questions with instant answers and explanations. Recognize indicators, understand reporting requirements.
whyItWorks: CTIP questions often ask you to spot indicators in a scenario rather than recall a flat fact, which is exactly where a quick second opinion helps most. Cambo reads the specific scenario in front of you and explains why an answer is right, not just what it is.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is a common indicator of human trafficking?
sampleQuestions.a: A person who does not have control of their own identification documents, such as a passport or ID card being held by someone else.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the DoD's 'zero tolerance' policy in regard to trafficking in persons?
sampleQuestions.a: DoD personnel are prohibited from engaging in any activity that supports or facilitates trafficking in persons, including using forced labor or patronizing commercial sex — with no exceptions.

faqs.q: How often is CTIP training required?
faqs.a: Initial training is required within the first year of DoD employment or service, with general awareness refresher training required every 2 years for all DoD personnel.

faqs.q: Who has to take CTIP training?
faqs.a: All DoD service members and civilian personnel, with additional specialized training for acquisition and contracting personnel who oversee contracts at risk of trafficking violations.

faqs.q: What should I do if I suspect trafficking?
faqs.a: Report it through your chain of command, the DoD Hotline, or local law enforcement — reporting channels are covered in detail during the training.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or the official CTIP program?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense.

faqs.q: What topics does CTIP training cover?
faqs.a: Definitions and forms of trafficking, indicators to watch for, DoD's zero-tolerance policy, and how to report suspected trafficking.

faqs.q: Does CTIP training apply to contractors?
faqs.a: Yes — contractors performing on DoD contracts, especially overseas, are subject to CTIP training and compliance requirements.
